parsed.justification: Rationale A correctly identifies the comment as containing an implicitly stated action (addressing the omission of anomaly segmentation) that is vague and lacks concrete implementation details, matching the score-2 description in the rubric. It grounds this assessment in the text and avoids unsupported claims. Rationale B correctly recognizes the comment as a clarification question rather than an explicit action, but it partially misapplies the rubric by treating clarification questions as outside the scoring framework, whereas the rubric explicitly states that clarification questions giving a direct action should be treated as explicit statements. B's analysis is also less precise about the implicit action (explaining design trade-offs) that can be inferred. Both rationales avoid unsupported claims, but B has a meaningful weakness in rubric correctness and decision coverage.
